description: A draft measurement vocabulary. Directions refer to the named measurement, not an unconditional goal. Units and rubrics must be fixed before comparison.

parameters.name: Time to accepted completion
parameters.definition: Elapsed time from task admission to externally accepted completion.
parameters.measurement: Record wall-clock duration and account for retrospective and verification overhead. Report unsuccessful runs separately with their consumed time.
parameters.limitations: A faster failed or prematurely stopped run is not an improvement. External waiting and active agent time should also be distinguishable.

parameters.name: Total token consumption
parameters.definition: All measured model tokens consumed by task execution and its required supporting work.
parameters.measurement: Sum execution, retrieval, retrospective and validation usage with an explicit accounting policy for input, output, cached and reasoning tokens.
parameters.limitations: Provider counters differ. Missing usage is unknown, not zero. Fewer tokens do not imply a better or cheaper result across models.

parameters.name: Total monetary cost
parameters.definition: Observed monetary expense attributable to a task and the supporting improvement process.
parameters.measurement: Use the same declared currency and pricing date; include measured API, compute and required validation costs. Report human time separately unless a rate was fixed beforehand.
parameters.limitations: Subscription opportunity costs and future amortization are assumptions. Do not treat an unbilled request as consuming no scarce resources.

parameters.name: Compute resource consumption
parameters.definition: Consumption of a specified compute resource under an agreed measurement boundary.
parameters.measurement: Choose CPU core-seconds, GPU-seconds, energy or another explicit resource before comparison; retain separate counters for unlike resources.
parameters.limitations: Hardware changes can invalidate comparisons. Do not add unlike resources into one unexplained number or infer utilization from elapsed time.

parameters.name: Result correctness
parameters.definition: Fraction of independently checked correctness requirements satisfied under a fixed task rubric.
parameters.measurement: Use acceptance tests or externally adjudicated criteria, preserving individual results and any hard failure condition.
parameters.limitations: Tests can be incomplete. A high average cannot excuse violation of a mandatory criterion. Agent self-assessment is not an independent validator.

parameters.name: Accepted task completeness
parameters.definition: Fraction of the original agreed deliverables accepted as completed.
parameters.measurement: Freeze the deliverable list and verify each item, including required delivery or deployment when in scope.
parameters.limitations: A status message alone does not prove delivery. Changing scope after a run can hide abandoned work. Correctness and completeness must both be checked.

parameters.name: Alignment with the requested goal
parameters.definition: Degree to which actions and outcomes satisfy the user's intended objective and explicit constraints.
parameters.measurement: Use a predeclared task-specific rubric evaluated against the original request and accepted clarifications.
parameters.limitations: Intent can be ambiguous and rubric judgments can disagree. Preserve disagreements rather than replacing the user's goal with an easily measured proxy.

parameters.name: Evidence coverage
parameters.definition: Fraction of material completion and performance claims linked to inspectable evidence.
parameters.measurement: Enumerate required claims and check the existence, relevance and reproducibility of their supporting artifacts.
parameters.limitations: More logs are not necessarily better evidence. Evidence existence does not establish authenticity or adequacy of the underlying test.

parameters.name: Autonomous accepted execution
parameters.definition: Fraction of eligible tasks completed correctly within the existing mandate without avoidable human intervention.
parameters.measurement: Fix which decisions are authorized and which legitimately require a person, then count avoidable intervention separately from required decisions.
parameters.limitations: Autonomy is bounded by authorization. Avoiding a required approval or silently reducing scope must never improve this score.

parameters.name: Control response reliability
parameters.definition: Fraction of authorized stop, correction, resume and rollback requests executed within the declared limits.
parameters.measurement: Exercise explicit control scenarios and record compliance, latency and unintended side effects.
parameters.limitations: This is scenario-bound. An acknowledgment is not evidence that the underlying process stopped or that its effects were reversed.

parameters.name: Constraint preservation
parameters.definition: Fraction of declared safety, authority and data-handling constraints preserved during execution.
parameters.measurement: Test named constraints and retain any critical violation as a hard failure independently of the aggregate fraction.
parameters.limitations: No observed violation does not establish safety beyond the tested scenarios. Do not trade mandatory constraints for a better average.

parameters.name: Outcome variability
parameters.definition: Dispersion of a declared outcome metric over equivalent repeated tasks and configurations.
parameters.measurement: Specify the outcome and dispersion estimator, report sample count and the complete outcome distribution where practical.
parameters.limitations: Consistent failure is predictable but undesirable. A variance estimate from too few runs is unstable and does not measure correctness.

parameters.name: Operational surface area
parameters.definition: Number of independently operated components required for the tested useful function.
parameters.measurement: Inventory mandatory processes, stores and externally managed services; also report configuration and operator steps when relevant.
parameters.limitations: A component count is a proxy. Merging components can hide coupling or increase maintenance burden. Compare the same useful functionality.

parameters.name: Capacity under fixed service constraints
parameters.definition: Sustained task throughput while meeting fixed correctness, latency and resource constraints.
parameters.measurement: Declare workload distribution, concurrency, resource budget and service constraints; measure steady-state throughput and tail behavior.
parameters.limitations: Short bursts or easier tasks do not prove scale. A single-machine prototype is not evidence of multi-terabyte corpus performance.

parameters.name: Recovery effectiveness
parameters.definition: Fraction of specified fault scenarios that preserve accepted outcomes or recover within declared bounds.
parameters.measurement: Inject bounded faults and check outcome integrity, recovery time, duplication and resource use.
parameters.limitations: Observed resilience applies to the injected faults. Retries can worsen non-transient failures or repeat irreversible actions.

parameters.name: Effort for a verified change
parameters.definition: Measured effort to implement and verify a comparable change in the system.
parameters.measurement: Use a fixed change task and count discovery, editing, testing and rework; distinguish human and automated effort.
parameters.limitations: Familiarity and task difficulty confound comparisons. Fewer files or lines do not establish maintainability by themselves.

parameters.name: Time to validated adaptation
parameters.definition: Elapsed time from a specified environmental change to a verified adequate response.
parameters.measurement: Introduce a declared change and measure detection, revised action and validation, including unnecessary changes made along the way.
parameters.limitations: Rapid unverified rewriting is not useful adaptation. The new solution must preserve protected constraints and have a known applicability scope.

parameters.name: Useful evidence retrieval
parameters.definition: Relevance of retrieved evidence to the current decision under a fixed relevance rubric.
parameters.measurement: Measure useful retrieved items and missed necessary items separately; retain provenance and the retrieval budget.
parameters.limitations: Precision alone can reward returning almost nothing. A relevance judgment does not prove a retrieved lesson is true or current.

parameters.name: Useful decision work per budget
parameters.definition: Verified decision value produced within a declared reasoning resource budget.
parameters.measurement: Predefine necessary decisions or discriminating experiments, judge whether they resolve uncertainty, and report consumed time or tokens separately.
parameters.limitations: This is a difficult research proxy, not an automatic transcript statistic. Long or short reasoning text alone does not establish value.

parameters.name: Beneficial reuse of prior evidence
parameters.definition: Fraction of eligible new task lineages for which using prior evidence yields an accepted, measured benefit.
parameters.measurement: Compare relevant reuse against a suitable control, include retrieval and update overhead, and count negative applications.
parameters.limitations: A frequently loaded rule is not necessarily helpful. Repeated copies of one task are not independent evidence of transfer.
